4_caption: Fig. 4. Cross-scale mutual feature aggregation (CMFA). Spatially aligned inputs A and B have equal projected width C = 256. (A) Their concatenation supplies a global-average-pooling and two-layer pointwise channel gate, which is split into gA and gB. (B) The gated inputs are exchanged through A + B ⊙ gB and B + A ⊙ gA, then concatenated. (C) Channel mean and maximum statistics of the concatenated feature produce a 7 × 7 sigmoid spatial gate. The output retains 2C = 512 channels. Cat denotes channel concatenation; circular multiplication and addition nodes operate elementwise.
5_caption: Fig. 5. High-order omni-attention (HOOA). (A) Local and dilated-context branches generate L and C; the high-pass input X − AvgPool₃(X) supplies an edge branch E. The second-order response L ⊙ sigmoid(C) is concatenated with L and E and projected to F. (B) Channel and spatial gates are both computed from F before gating. Their product modulates F, and the update is added to X with bounded scale α = 0.30 sigmoid(s). DW and PW denote depthwise and pointwise convolutions. Local and edge convolutions include batch normalization and SiLU; the context branch uses SiLU after its depthwise convolution and batch normalization after its final pointwise convolution. Spatial statistics are channel-wise mean and maximum. Tensor glyphs illustrate feature shape, not measured response maps.
